description:
A router/demux node that inspects buffer type or header metadata at runtime and forwards to the correct downstream node. Unlike the existing zstreamer filter (which routes on a boolean condition), this routes to one of N possible children based on content type.

Use cases:
- Receiving a mixed audio stream and routing MP3 frames to an MP3 decoder, Matroska containers to a Matroska demuxer, raw PCM to a direct output path
- A network source receiving different media types on the same socket
- A file source reading containers with multiple embedded codecs

Design considerations:
- Routing table: map buffer_type -> child device, configurable at runtime
- Default/fallback route for unknown types
- Must integrate with buffer typing (zstreamer-33y) for type identification
- Could be implemented as a new node type (router) or as an extension of the filter node
- Should support registering new routes at runtime (for dynamic node loading)
title: Dynamic routing by buffer type

description:
A pre-allocated single-thread worker pool that handles dynamic node dispatch at runtime. Instead of spawning/destroying threads per codec, a single dedicated worker thread picks up jobs from a queue — each job is a different processing function (e.g. MP3 demux, Matroska demux, PCM passthrough).

## Design

**Work queue pattern:**
- One persistent thread with a pre-allocated stack (like Zephyr k_work_q)
- A queue of work items, each carrying: buffer pointer, process() callback, context pointer
- The worker thread dequeues and executes the appropriate process() for each buffer
- Memory for work items is pre-allocated from a fixed pool (k_mem_slab or static array) — no runtime malloc

**How it integrates with dynamic routing:**
1. Dynamic router inspects buffer type
2. Looks up the registered process() callback for that type
3. Submits a work item: {buffer, process_fn, node_ctx} to the worker queue
4. Worker thread executes process_fn(node_ctx, buffer) and forwards the result

**Pre-reserved memory:**
- Worker thread stack: single ZSTREAMER_THREAD_STACK_SIZE allocation at compile time
- Work item pool: fixed-size slab of N work item structs (configurable via Kconfig)
- Node contexts: each registered "virtual node" gets a pre-allocated context struct with its state, but no dedicated thread or stack
- This means 10 different demux nodes share 1 thread + 1 stack, with only their context structs taking separate memory

**Advantages over thread-per-node:**
- Deterministic memory usage — all reserved at compile time
- No thread create/destroy overhead at runtime
- Scales to many node types without linear stack cost (10 nodes × 2KB = 20KB saved vs 1 × 2KB shared)
- Natural backpressure via queue depth

**Key considerations:**
- Sequential processing: only one demux runs at a time on the worker thread — acceptable if demux is not the bottleneck
- Priority: worker thread priority must be chosen carefully (probably same as normal node threads)
- If parallel demux is ever needed, can extend to a thread pool (N workers) without changing the API
title: Runtime node worker pool

description:
Design a mechanism for any node along the pipeline to attach arbitrary key-value or typed metadata to a buffer as it flows through. Unlike the fixed creation metadata (set once by the source), this is mutable and extensible.

Options to investigate:
1. **Reserved region in user_data**: partition user_data into fixed header + flexible tail. Nodes write into known offsets. Simple but rigid — total size fixed at compile time.
2. **Linked metadata via net_buf frags**: attach a secondary net_buf as a fragment containing metadata. Nodes can append frags. Flexible but adds allocation overhead.
3. **Side-channel metadata map**: maintain a separate per-buffer metadata store (e.g. indexed by buffer pool index) that nodes can write to. Avoids touching net_buf layout but adds lookup cost.
4. **Typed metadata slots**: compile-time registered metadata types with known sizes and offsets in user_data. Nodes declare which metadata types they produce/consume. Gives type safety with zero runtime overhead.

Considerations:
- Must work with both net_buf_ref (shared readonly) and net_buf_clone (writable copy)
- For ref-shared buffers, metadata mutations would need COW or be prohibited
- Should integrate with buffer typing system (zstreamer-33y) for type-specific metadata
- Memory budget: user_data size is fixed per pool, so flexible approaches should not waste space for nodes that do not use them
title: Generic per-node pipeline metadata

description:
Define a standard fixed metadata struct stored in net_buf user_data[], set once at buffer allocation time by the source node. Fields should include:
- creator: pointer to the originating device (source node)
- timestamp: k_uptime_ticks() at allocation time
- sequence number: monotonically increasing per-source counter
- buffer_id: unique ID (pool index or atomic counter)
- sample_rate / frame_size: for audio sources (optional, typed via buffer typing later)

Implementation: increase the user_data_size in GRAPH_POOL_DEFINE from 0 to sizeof(struct zstreamer_buf_meta). Populate in zstreamer_node_alloc_buf() or a new zstreamer_source_alloc_buf() wrapper. Must be zero-overhead for nodes that do not read metadata (just ignore user_data). net_buf_clone() already copies user_data, so cloned buffers inherit the creation metadata automatically.
title: Fixed buffer creation metadata
